title: Addressing Lying in the Child Aged Seven to Nine
text_original: في هذا العمر يدرك الطفل معنى الكذب، وغالباً يكذب خوفاً من العقاب أو رغبةً في الظهور أو تجنّب الإحراج. ابحثي عن السبب وراء الكذبة بدل الاكتفاء بمعاقبتها. وضّحي له بهدوء أثر الكذب على الثقة بين الناس، واربطيه بقيمة الصدق في ديننا وأن الصدق يهدي إلى البر. تجنّبي نصب الفخاخ له بأسئلة تعرفين إجابتها لتوقعيه في الكذب. كافئي الصدق واجعلي الاعتراف بالخطأ مخرجاً آمناً يخفّف العقوبة. كوني صادقة في وعودك معه فالطفل يفقد الصدق حين يرى الكبار يكذبون. إن كان الكذب متكرراً ومقلقاً فابحثي عن ضغط أو خوف يدفعه إليه.
text_simplified: At this age, the child understands the meaning of lying and often lies out of fear of punishment, a desire to impress, or to avoid embarrassment. Look for the reason behind the lie instead of merely punishing it. Explain to him calmly the effect of lying on trust between people, and connect it to the value of truthfulness in our religion, that 'truthfulness leads to righteousness (al-birr).' Avoid setting traps for him with questions you already know the answers to in order to catch him lying. Reward truthfulness and make admitting mistakes a safe way out that lessens the punishment. Be truthful in your promises with him, for the child loses truthfulness when he sees adults lying. If the lying is repeated and concerning, look for pressure or fear that may be driving him to it.

review_defects.why: The Arabic means 'to make him fall into lying' (i.e., to induce him to lie), but the English says 'to catch him lying', which changes the purpose from causing the lie to detecting it.

review_defects.english: may be driving him to it
review_defects.why: The Arabic is definite ('drives him to it'), but the English adds 'may be', introducing uncertainty not present in the source.
